observedMismatch.surface: normal user-facing ONE PIECE Home phone mockup
observedMismatch.fact: The indicator was absolutely positioned but rendered a solid rgba(247,244,233,.94) strip across the screen bottom, visually behaving like an appended footer.

qaMiss.reason: Prior QA checked position and scroll stability but did not reject a solid full-width indicator background that visually became a footer.

feedback: Why is there spacing above the bottom edge?
Why add a white translucent gradient?
userCorrectionRevision2.rootCause: The implementation and first fresh QA reused a Pokémon-derived contrast treatment without ONE PIECE evidence. They optimized bar visibility and non-overlap but failed the necessity test: neither a white veil nor a full indicator-height blank band was required.
userCorrectionRevision2.decision: Use a fully transparent indicator container, anchor it to the chassis bottom, retain only the black bar, and reduce content inset to the minimum needed for clearance.

correctiveAction: Inset the outer indicator horizontally by the measured chassis border and anchor it to the chassis bottom.
Use a fully transparent indicator container; only the black bar may be visible.
Reduce final document safe inset below the indicator height while retaining minimum clearance.
Keep explicit no-shell proof modes free of the indicator.

preventiveGate.basis: The same chassis-vs-document ownership failure appeared in both brands; the ONE PIECE follow-up additionally proves that a generic contrast gradient and full-height safe band can themselves become unsupported chrome.
